name: What inspections should I expect during ADU construction, and what happens if something fails?

mainEntity.name: What inspections should I expect during ADU construction, and what happens if something fails?

acceptedAnswer.text:
You can expect multiple inspections throughout an ADU build, typically including foundation, framing, rough plumbing and electrical, insulation, and final inspection. Inspectors verify the work matches approved plans and code; if something fails, the contractor must correct it and call for a reinspection. 

Inspections may feel stressful, but they are your safeguard against hidden issues that could haunt you later.

Key factors:
- Sequence of inspections tied to major construction milestones
- Role of city/county inspector vs third‑party special inspections (if needed)
- Documentation: approved plans, correction notices, and sign‑offs
- Impact of failed inspections on schedule and cost

Ask your builder to share the anticipated inspection schedule and who meets inspectors on site. If a phase fails, insist on seeing what was corrected before it’s covered, so you know problems are resolved properly and not rushed just to pass.
acceptedAnswer.description: ADU projects go through several inspections—foundation, framing, rough trades, insulation, and final—to confirm work meets plans and code. If something fails, your contractor must fix it and schedule a reinspection. Treat inspections as quality checks and ask to see any corrections before they’re covered.
